title: Nav urgency pill counts findings that are snoozed until later
body:
## Summary
getDirectorStats.openCriticalHigh counts critical/high findings whose snooze has not lapsed, though the type says a snooze hides the finding until snoozedUntil.

## Description
src/lib/game-director-db.ts:688-693 filters only TRIAGE_EXCLUDED_SQL (false-positive, ignore), so an active snooze counts as open. The read path derives snooze expiry at read time in rowToFinding (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:906-915) and the type doc (src/types/game-director.ts:16-19) says snooze 'hides it until snoozedUntil expires'. The SQL count cannot see that derivation, so the nav 'All Findings' pill and the list disagree. Fixed = openCriticalHigh adds `AND NOT (triage_status = 'snooze' AND snoozed_until > now)`; the scoring counts stay as documented.

## Flow
- snooze a critical finding for 7 days
- nav pill still counts it; the list hides it
- after fix: pill drops by 1 until the snooze lapses

## Expected impact
Operators stop chasing a pill that points at findings they parked. Could break: anyone reading the pill as 'all unresolved incl. parked'.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - urgency pill counts what the list shows as open
Before: walked: 1 future-snoozed critical -> openCriticalHigh 1, visible open list 0
After: predicted: openCriticalHigh 0 until snoozed_until passes, then 1
Method: simulation - whether 'open' excludes a parked snooze is a product reading; a db test decides the mechanics
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: db test: seed a critical with snoozed_until=+7d and one with -1d, assert openCriticalHigh counts only the lapsed one

title: Say when All Findings is truncated at 200
body:
## Summary
getAllFindings returns the newest 200 findings with no total, so FindingsExplorer silently shows a partial set as if complete.

## Description
src/lib/game-director-db.ts:597-603 hardcodes `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 200`; src/app/api/game-director/route.ts:191-194 returns the array as-is; src/components/modules/game-director/FindingsExplorer/index.tsx:67 filters and counts it. Past 200 findings every count and filter in the explorer is over a truncated sample with no signal (software-engineering/bounded-enumeration: a bounded read says it is bounded). Fixed = return a total alongside, and the explorer shows 'newest 200 of N'.

## Flow
- accumulate 201+ findings across sessions
- open All Findings: counts read 200, no notice
- after fix: header reads 'newest 200 of 201'

## Expected impact
Designers triaging a large backlog know the view is partial. Could break: the route's array contract (pof-mcp and tests read it).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a bounded list states its bound
Before: simulation: 201 seeded findings -> explorer count 200, 0 truncation signals
After: predicted: 1 truncation signal with total 201
Method: simulation - needs a route + component change outside the db file; the instrument is a 201-row seed
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: seed 201 findings in a throwaway DB, call GET action=all-findings, assert a total/truncated field and the explorer notice

title: Validate the summary the writer API's complete action stores
body:
## Summary
POST /api/game-director action=complete writes the caller's summary unchecked, so a missing or non-numeric overallScore lands on a completed session.

## Description
src/app/api/game-director/route.ts:276-291 destructures `summary` as PlaytestSummary and passes it to updateSessionSummary (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:421-437) with no shape check. Commit d86505b2 made every READ ignore such a session (SCORED_SESSION_SQL), but the row is still marked complete with a summary every consumer types as carrying a number. Fixed = 400 when overallScore is not a finite 0-100 number. The route is outside this context's declared file_paths.

## Flow
- external harness POSTs complete with summary {}
- session shows complete with no score, typed as having one
- after fix: 400 naming summary.overallScore

## Expected impact
External writers are told at write time instead of producing a silently unscored session. Could break: a harness that posts partial summaries.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - reject a malformed completed summary at the boundary
Before: walked: complete with summary {} -> 200, row complete, overallScore absent
After: predicted: 400 naming the field, row unchanged
Method: simulation - route is out of this round's paths (veto 1)
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: route test: POST complete with summary {} and with overallScore 'x' -> expect 400

title: One bad scan timestamp turns the whole project-health POST into a 500
body:
## Summary
generateQualityHistory calls new Date(scan.timestamp).toISOString(), which throws RangeError for one unparseable timestamp and fails the entire health computation.

## Description
src/lib/health-engine.ts:86-87 maps every scan through `new Date(scan.timestamp).toISOString()`. An invalid date throws RangeError: Invalid time value; src/app/api/project-health/route.ts catches it as 500 'Health computation failed', so Holistic Health loses every signal because of one persisted scan. Fixed = skip and count scans whose timestamp is not finite, the way weeklyCompletionSeries counts undated completions. health-engine.ts is outside this context's paths.

## Flow
- evaluator scanHistory holds one scan with timestamp 'n/a'
- POST /api/project-health -> 500
- after fix: 200, quality history omits that scan and reports it skipped

## Expected impact
Holistic Health keeps rendering when one stored scan is malformed. Could break: tests that expect every scan to appear.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a bad record degrades one series, not the whole summary
Before: walked: 1 of N scans with an invalid timestamp -> RangeError -> 500
After: predicted: 200 with N-1 quality points
Method: simulation - file is in another context (veto 1)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test: computeProjectHealth with scanHistory [{timestamp:'n/a', ...}] must not throw

title: Guard TERM_GLOSSARY lookups against Object.prototype keys
body:
## Summary
The layout-lab term lookup indexes a plain object literal unguarded, the defect already fixed in lookupCrashTerm and (this round) lookupGlossary.

## Description
src/components/layout-lab/labGlossary.ts:63 returns `TERM_GLOSSARY[term.toLowerCase()] ?? null`; after lower-casing, 'constructor' and '__proto__' still resolve to inherited Object members and come back typed as a GlossaryEntry. Siblings fixed: src/lib/crash-glossary.ts (src/__tests__/lib/crash-glossary-prototype-keys.test.ts) and src/lib/ecw/glossary.ts (bbfeab9e). Fixed = Object.hasOwn guard. Out of this context's paths (catalog pipeline).

## Flow
- call the lab term lookup with 'constructor'
- returns Object's constructor function as a GlossaryEntry
- after fix: null

## Expected impact
The third copy of the rule agrees with the other two. Could break: nothing in-tree passes such keys today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule for glossary lookups across the three dictionaries
Before: read: 2 of 3 glossary lookups guarded
After: predicted: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - catalog-pipeline path is out of this round's scope
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Write one timestamp spelling and order events by instant
body:
## Summary
Director rows mix two timestamp spellings in the same columns, and getEvents orders the event timeline by the raw TEXT.

## Description
completed_at is ISO from updateSessionStatus (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:397-399) but datetime('now') from updateSessionSummary (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:428-431); events default to datetime('now') (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:255) while external-ingest writes ISO (src/lib/game-director/external-ingest.ts:310). getEvents (src/lib/game-director-db.ts:625) orders by timestamp TEXT, where 'T' (0x54) sorts after ' ' (0x20), so mixed spellings within the same second-range mis-order. adc93dd4 normalised the READ projection only. Fixed = ORDER BY datetime(timestamp) DESC, rowid DESC (as SESSION_CHRONOLOGY does) and one write spelling.

## Flow
- add an event with the default timestamp and one ISO-stamped 1 s earlier
- timeline shows text order, not time order
- after fix: time order

## Expected impact
Timeline and any completed_at sort read in instant order. Could break: nothing visible if every writer already stamps ISO.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - chronological reads compare instants, not spellings
Before: walked: ISO '...T10:00:00.000Z' vs default '... 10:00:01' -> the ISO row sorts newer
After: predicted: the default (10:00:01) row sorts newer
Method: simulation - the reachable mix depends on which writers omit timestamp; a two-row db test decides it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: db test: two events one second apart in the two spellings; assert getEvents order

title: Context map entry for game-director-system misstates its surface
body:
## Summary
context-map.json says the context serves GET/POST /api/project-health and omits src/components/modules/game-director/ from file_paths.

## Description
src/app/api/project-health/route.ts exports POST only. The map's file_paths list 12 files but not the game-director component tree named as its entry point, so file-scoped rounds (this one) never read the Director UI; .ai/registry-map.json paths do include it. Fixed = Personas context rescan (context-map.json is director-owned).

## Flow
- read context-map.json game-director-system api_surface and file_paths
- compare with the route's exports and registry-map paths

## Expected impact
Next rounds scope the Director UI they currently skip. Could break: nothing; metadata.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the context map matches the code
Before: 1 wrong api_surface verb, 1 entry-point directory missing from file_paths
After: 0 mismatches after rescan
Method: probe - read both files; the fix is an operator-only rescan
Result: better
Gate: direction
